text: Vague longing and boredom are close akin.
plain: Restless wanting and boredom are the same itch.

text: When a man is dead, we envy him no more; and we only half envy him when he is old.
plain: Envy fades once the race is over.

text: Misanthropy and love of solitude are convertible ideas.
plain: Hating people and loving being alone are close to the same thing.

text: What makes us almost inevitably ridiculous is our serious way of treating the passing moment, as though it necessarily had all the importance which it seems to have.
plain: You take today's problem way too seriously.

text: Life is a language in which certain truths are conveyed to us; could we learn them in some other way, we should not live.
plain: Some things you only learn by living through them.

text: As a rule, the fear of the ills we know drive us into the contrary ills; the pain of solitude, for example, drives us into society, and the first society that comes; the discomforts of society drive us into solitude; we exchange a forbidding demeanour for incautious confidence and so on.
plain: Running from one pain, you crash into its opposite. Don't overcorrect.

text: A good supply of resignation is of the first importance in providing for the journey of life. It is a supply which we shall have to extract from disappointed hopes; and the sooner we do it, the better for the rest of the journey.
plain: Learn to accept letdowns early. It makes the rest of the road easier.

text: We seldom think of what we have, but always of what we lack.
plain: You stare at what's missing and forget what you hold.

text: On the heights we must expect to be solitary.
plain: Climbing high means being alone up there.

text: Habit is everything.
plain: What you repeat is what you become.

text: Marriage is a trap which nature sets for us.
plain: Nature wants you paired up whether it suits you or not.

text: If the object is to render the pupil a better man by telling him that others are excellent, it fails; and it would be more to the purpose to say: Most men are bad, it is for you to be better.
plain: Don't expect others to be good. Be better yourself.

text: If we were not all of us exaggeratedly interested in ourselves, life would be so uninteresting that no one could endure it.
plain: Self-obsession is what keeps life interesting enough to bear.

text: Why should it be folly to be always intent on getting the greatest possible enjoyment out of the moment, which is our only sure possession? Our whole life is no more than a magnified present, and in itself as fleeting.
plain: The present is all you actually own. Use it.

text: The only genuine superiority is that of the mind and character; all other kinds are fictitious, affected, false; and it is good to make them feel that it is so when they try to show off before the superiority that is true.
plain: Only mind and character make you better than anyone. Rank and show are fake.

text: A man is wise only on condition of living in a world full of fools.
plain: Wisdom is only visible against everyone else's foolishness.

text: We must always try to preserve large views. If we are arrested by details we shall get confused, and see things awry. The success or the failure of the moment, and the impression that they make, should count for nothing.
plain: Zoom out. Today's win or loss barely matters.

text: How difficult it is to learn to understand oneself, and clearly to recognise what it is that one wants before anything else; what it is, therefore, that is most immediately necessary to our happiness; then what comes next; and what takes the third and the fourth place, and so on.
plain: Rank what you want. Without that you drift.

text: The man who understands how to pat his fellows best, though they be the nastiest brutes,--that's the man who has many friends.
plain: A big circle usually means flattery, not merit.

text: It is the longest pendulum that makes the greatest swing. Little minds soon come to terms with themselves and the world, and then fossilise; but the others flourish, and are always alive and in motion.
plain: Big people struggle longer. Settling early is how you stop growing.

text: It is a persistent, uninterrupted activity that constitutes the superior mind.
plain: Greatness is relentless work, not a flash.
